claims.statement: The native UI (t3k::ui) laid out every screen in the fixed design space of core/Design.h: kWidth = 1024, kHeight = 578 (content only; Figma's 600 includes a 22px mock titlebar), plus chrome strips that grow the window instead of squishing the core: kBannerHeight=44, kHintHeight=36, kHeaderHeight=45, kPlateHeight=108; kMaxScale = 2.0 (editor corner-drag scale ceiling). NativeEditor applies a single AffineTransform so no child component ever sees window size — this is a port of useUiScale.ts (1 design px = 1 JUCE logical unit).

Services (services/Services.h) is the per-editor bundle of stores: UiClock (one 30 Hz tick every poller shares), ChainStore (revision-poll + optimistic edits), MeterStore, PresetStore, AudioDeviceStore (standalone only), MidiMapStore, UiPrefs, HintBus, Toast, Banners, ParamBinding, AutoMeasure, SpectrumFeed, TunerFeed, ModelLoads, LocalFiles, ImageLoader, ConnectionGate, UpdateCheck, ToneLoadFlow, Zoom, Pointer, and the TONE3000 cloud stack (HttpClient, OAuth, LoopbackServer, Tone3000Client, Tone3000Session). Ownership: NativeEditor → Services → PluginRoot → views; views hold references to the services they use and register as listeners in the constructor / unregister in the destructor. No singletons: two editors in one process never see each other's state.

The testbed (plugin/ui/testbed) is a standalone JUCE app (UiTestbed) that renders PluginRoot against a fixture-driven MockBackend + MockSession: --scenario for live windows, --capture [refDir] for 2x PNG screenshots + diff tables, --compare before/after for single pairs, --selftest for unit tests (pure logic + focus policy in a real window), --bench [--seconds N] [--json] for CPU / memory under realistic phase loads. Its own project keeps UI iteration from rebuilding the DSP tree; -DT3K_BUILD_UI_TESTBED=ON on the plugin build registers --selftest with ctest (CI runs it next to the DSP suite).

The view tree from NativeEditor (owns UiPrefs, HttpClient, Tone3000Session, Services, PluginRoot; scales the 1024-wide design space) is: PluginRoot → PluginHeader (PresetBar / AccountMenu / StereoModeToggle) + AppBanner + middle (MainScreen chain + faceplate | BlockCard for a single-block detail view | TunerView; ToneBrowser takes over middle + Faceplate while open; SignInScreen takes that slot while signing in) + Faceplate + HintBar + OverlayLayer (Settings, modals, popovers, Toast). BlockCard (views/block/BlockCard.h) is the per-block card (Tone + Mix + power) that syncHeader() re-selects its tone without recreating the in-flight handler's closure, per the data flow rule.

The reverb tile's Dry knob uses scales::reverbDry(), a standalone scale that mirrors scales::convGain() exactly (toDisplay linear-maps 0..1 to -24..+24 dB, toStored/fromStored are the identity, format renders signed dB). It is a separate scale so reverb-tile and conv-tile each name their own dry face independently; the conv tile's convDry knob keeps using scales::convGain().

The two SIG slots (Air row 1, Early row 2) are re-voiced per mode by reverbSigParam/Label/ScaleForMode. numParams_ for the reverb face = 8 engine params + Mix + Out chain-level entries. COMPRESSOR TYPE CYCLER (commit 3ffb35b; label order fixed 2026-10-14, commit 5f93ab9): the full compressor tile carries a per-mode TYPE cycler button (typeCycle_, a juce::TextButton) that mirrors the reverb tile's type cycler. Bounds (resized(), full view): typeCycle_ at (W - 14 - 44, 44, 44, 26) — right of the mode selector, which slides left to modeCombo_ (W - 14 - 44 - 8 - 120, 44, 120, 26); both share the y=44 band. It is HIDDEN in the compact tile (typeCycle_.setVisible(!compact_)) because the compact header's free slot (65..95) belongs to the PUNCH toggle and 28..62 to the mode cycler, and with one self-type per mode the cycler is a one-entry no-op until a mode gains a second type. Button text = compactCompTypeName(block_.compMode, compType): the self-type labels in ENGINE-index order {VCA, TUB, OPT, FET, VMU} (0=VCA 1=Tube 2=Opto 3=FET 4=Vari-Mu; the 5f93ab9 fix reordered the array from the old display order {… VMU, FET} so the chip text matches the loaded engine — FET is the 1176, Vari-Mu the 670). Help text = help::text(help::Key::compType) (a Key in Help.h, desktop blurb in Help.cpp) + a per-mode compTypeBlurb ("general-purpose VCA -- smooth RMS soft-knee compression" / "Tube-STA -- warm tube detector, the output-stage saturation" / "Opto-2A -- two-stage optical cells, ratio-dependent slow attack" / "FET -- four-amp sum, fast transient grab + stage coloration" / "Vari-Mu 670 -- release-position ladder, feedback detection, odd-only crunch"); the compMode help text in Help.cpp distinguishes FET (the 1176 four-amp feedback detector) from Vari-Mu (the Fairchild 670 release-position ladder). onClick opens a PopupMenu listing i in [0, Compressor::numTypes(m)) as "<label> — <blurb>" (current checked) and calls enterCompType(choice-1). syncCompTypeButton(m) re-syncs button + help text (called from enterMode); enterCompType(type) is a no-op if type == compTypeOf(block_), else sets block_.compType VERBATIM (the engine clamps via setParams/numTypes) and calls services().chain.setBlockParam(blockId(), "compType", (double)type), then syncCompTypeButton.

The 2026-10-14 swappable-theme change converted the Theme.h colour tokens from compile-time constants to mutable `inline juce::Colour` globals, added `struct ThemePalette` (a snapshot of every token), and `applyPalette(const ThemePalette&)` / `resetPalette()` which restore the defaults. The live (NativeEditor/Processor) UI always uses the defaults; palette swapping is a testbed-only feature (TileShot/UiTestbed), so the shipped plugin looks unchanged.

The 2026-10-14 OCR capture mode adds `--ocr` to TileShot (and UiTestbed capture): it calls `theme::applyPalette(theme::ocrPalette())` before building the component (and `resetPalette()` after) to render a black-on-white high-contrast variant where the 12px type-chip labels become machine-readable. `theme::ocrPalette()` (a function-local static in Theme.h) maps brandBlue/Yellow/Red and linkBlue to black and all dark-surface tokens to white. `script/tile-ocr.sh` shoots a tile with `--ocr`, crops a button region by design coordinates, up-scales + binarizes, and reads it with Tesseract (psm 7/13/10, char whitelist A-Z) — the measured pass bar is the comp-shift type chip reading its model letter.

The swappable-theme ticket added test/src/theme_palette_tests.cpp to DspTests, which compiles the real plugin/ui/core/Theme.h and guards the palette contract: the default palette round-trips through applyPalette/resetPalette, and ocrPalette() inverts the brand colours to black while keeping white text on white surfaces.

DspTests compiles the real plugin DSP sources plus exactly FIVE plugin/ui files: plugin/ui/core/Labels.cpp (the KnobScale readout formatter the scale-contract tests link), plugin/ui/views/nodeview/NodeModel.cpp + plugin/ui/model/ChainState.cpp (the node grid's read-side model and its data source), and plugin/ui/views/gallery/EffectParams.cpp (added 6813cb5 so the wave/volume paramsFor branches are compile-checked by the real test link) — everything else in plugin/ui (views, services, paint) is excluded; a green DspTests does NOT prove the UI links (verify UI changes with the Standalone/VST3 build or the UiTestbed testbed).

Conv Start/End faces use scales::convTrimScale(b.convRawSeconds) (KnobScale.h:675): a per-IR linear 0..cap-second scale (2 dp, 's') whose cap is the raw IR length rounded UP to whole seconds (jlimit 1..999 — a sub-second IR gets a 1 s face, not 0), cached in a static unordered_map<int, KnobScale> keyed by the whole-second cap. The stored domain is seconds in every case (no toStored split, mirroring the delay/chorus time knobs). Reason (m04334 item 5, spec spc-1792564638419-71605): the old fixed convStart()/convEnd() 0..10 s faces let the user trim PAST the tail of a short IR, and an empty/past-tail trim window silently kept serving the old kernel; the face cap must track the loaded IR. This is also where the on-load defaults depend on the face knowing the IR length (Start=0 / End=IR-length set in ProcessorChain::loadConvIr, plus the strip's IR-length-change rebuild — see the node-view page). Wired at EffectParams.cpp:155-158 as the Start/End scales of the conv full param table (tile and strip share paramsFor).

CONV FULL-TILE FACE (commit 44a78ea face rework; Start/End per-IR caps + shared curve band + _exported_ name as of 9a5c3c8/9c203cb): the convolution full tile's face is a 7-col grid — ROW 1 = Mix (chain-level) | Dwell | Dry | Time | Pre | Start | End; ROW 2 = Width | Mod | F In | F Out | Out (chain-level). The 'In' input_ knob is relabelled Dwell and re-scaled to scales::convDwell() (KnobScale.h:634 — a +-18..+18 dB DISPLAY window over the SAME inputGainNormalized store, identity toStored/fromStored, signed-dB format; the engine law (s-0.5)*48 dB at Processor.cpp means knob 0.25..0.75 = -12..+12 dB, the window is clamped so the face is a readable sub-range). Start/End on the face use the per-IR scales::convTrimScale(b.convRawSeconds) (see that claim) — the old fixed convStart()/convEnd() 0..10 s scales are gone, and the old separate Settings view is gone. Wave/Volume EXACT-FACE law (m08349, commit 6d99a30; supersedes the 6813cb5 trio-bearing wave/volume sections): both kinds spawn at 100% mix and their faces carry NO Mix/In/Out trio — the wave tile face is just the Output (waveLevel, waveLevel() 0..100%) and Shape (waveShape() 5 detents sine/triangle/saw-up/saw-down/square) row, and the volume tile a single Volume knob (scales::gainDb()).
